To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the bending energy for a landmarked image with edgels is a quadratic form in the landmark positions and the edge directions, and (2) the edge directions are a basis for the bending energy, orthogonal to the basis of landmark displacements.

(1) the thin-plate energy for a set of points in the plane can be extended to a set of pairs of points in the neighborhood of a given curve and (2) this extension can be used to derive a set of edge deformations that are orthogonal to landmark deformations and to each other, and which can be interpreted as changes in edge direction without movement of the underlying landmarks.

(i) the thin-plate bending energy for landmarks is a special case of the bending energy of edgels; (ii) the edgel bending energy has a spectrum of eigenfunctions that is the union of the landmark spectrum and a new set of edge features; (iii) these edge features correspond to infinitesimal rotations of the landmark configuration, with the edge direction as the rotation axis; and (iv) the edge features have a well-defined interpretation in the context of image warping.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extension of the landmark-based approach to incorporate edge information.
the development of an efficient and effective method for the extraction and analysis of shape and edge information in medical images.
the development of a mathematical framework for the description of images in terms of their landmark and edgel configurations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed feature space provides an effective and useful tool for the comparison and classification of anatomical structures in medical images.
the new approach provides a useful extension of the thin- plate spline for landmark analysis, and that it is well worth the effort to use it in applications.
the edge warps, in combination with the landmark deformations, form a basis for the deformations of images that are consistent with a given landmark model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the finite-dimensional approach is extended to include edge features, and the edge features are interpreted as infinitesimal deformations of landmarks.
we have developed a feature space for edgel pairs that are constrained to lie on landmarks.
the thin-plate energy is the appropriate energy for landmark deformations, while the bending energy for edgels is an appropriate energy for edge deformations, and that the two are orthogonal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the feature space of edge warps, which we call edgels, is finite-dimensional and can be computed explicitly.

the edge information is a natural complement to the landmark information, and that the combination of both types of information is a natural way to extend the thin-plate splines to the edge information.
edge information can be incorporated into a finite-dimensional framework for image deformations, and that the resulting edge warps have a natural basis that is well-suited for statistical analysis.
